text:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT TRIGGERED: spike in 5xx from edge -> model-proxy (error-rate > 8% over 5m). Paging sam-oncall and irene-sre.

sam-oncall: on it, joining. seeing 502/504s in the dashboard. customers reporting gateway errors.

irene-sre: I can see the same in the edge-metrics: p50 latency stable, but p95 and 5xx increased sharply at 13:08 UTC. top upstream: inference-proxy and model-cache.

mike-runtime: recent deploy? deploy-bot: deploy edge-proxy v3.2.1 to canary at 13:05 UTC (tag: ev-proxy-canary).

sam-oncall: okay, likely related. rolling canary tweak earlier: route weight redistribution for /v1/generate to new shard. maybe misrouted traffic.

leo-support: we have multiple customer tickets: logs show `Gateway Error (504)` when calling /v1/chat and `upstream prematurely closed connection`.

irene-sre: dump of envoy config shows a new retry policy on route that adds 3 retries and retry_on: 5xx,connect,reset. that could be amplifying load. snippet:

```
route:
  match: prefix "/v1/generate"
  route:
    cluster: inference-proxy-canary
    retry_policy:
      retry_on: "5xx,connect,reset"
      num_retries: 3
```

sam-oncall: those retries look dangerous to enable without circuit breaker tuned. What are current cb settings?

mike-runtime: circuit-breaker config for inference-proxy-canary: max_connections 100, max_pending 100, max_requests 200. traffic to canary is currently 40% due to mistake in rollout script. intended 5% but weight set to 40.

sam-oncall: ah. two problems: high route weight to a canary with low cb, plus retries enabled. that will cascade 5xx -> retries -> upstream OOM/conn close -> more 5xx.

irene-sre: immediate mitigation options: 1) reduce route weight to 0 for canary 2) disable route-level retries 3) increase CB thresholds (short-term) 4) divert traffic to healthy cluster.

sam-oncall: let's do option 1 + 2 now. mike, can you set canary weight to 0 in the load balancer? I can remove retry policy via ADS.

mike-runtime: doing weight -> 0 now. running: `kubectl patch configmap edge-routes -p '{"data":{"/v1/generate":"weight:0"}}'` (applied). verifying...

deploy-bot: config pushed to edge-config-service. CDS/EDS update sent to Envoy xDS.

sam-oncall: removing retry policy for the route. applying patch to envoy route config to remove retry_policy.

irene-sre: watching metrics... 30s after change error-rate dropping from 8.2% -> 3.1%. p95 latency also improving.

leo-support: customer reports fewer errors, some successful retries cleared. we'll update tickets.

mike-runtime: cb thresholds left as-is for now. we can increase max_connections to 500 if needed but that risks overload on canary. since weight=0, not necessary.

sam-oncall: good. keep weight 0 until we validate canary resource limits and add proper CB + rate shaping. Next steps: rollback canary to last stable image in the deploy pipeline and re-run canary with 5% weight + proper CB tuning.

anna-product: quick note: any notion of customer-facing blip? should we send an incident banner?

leo-support: impact window ~13:05-13:15 UTC, ~10 minutes, affecting ~0.8% of total api calls but hitting some high-value customers. recommend banner and postmortem.

sam-oncall: agreed. I'll create an incident page and set severity P2. irene, mike, please do a short RCA draft (what config change, wrong rollout script parameter, missing CB tuning, retries enabled).

irene-sre: will gather logs and xds diffs. I found the root cause: a CI job accidentally updated the rollout weight var (missing env check).

mike-runtime: I'll add a guard in the rollout script to prevent >10% unless a manual flag is provided. also add monitor to alert on weight changes >5% within 10min.

deploy-bot: canary rollback initiated to ev-proxy v3.1.9.

sam-oncall: thanks everyone. I'll keep channel open for updates and the incident page. postmortem owners: irene + mike. tagging @anna-product for customer comms. :thumbsup:

pagerbot: Incident acknowledged by sam-oncall. Incident status: MITIGATED (traffic reverted, retries removed).

sam-oncall: closing thread once postmortem and banner drafted.
